open_obligations: Check which assumptions (rho-stability, A-provability) prover-estimator debate adds relative to doubly-efficient debate.
Note the shift from deterministic worst-case guarantees to average-case guarantees.
Verify the cost comparison assumes q constant and q^d = O(n^c).
in.other_title: Prover-estimator debate mitigates the obfuscated arguments problem in recursive debate
in.rationale: Brown-Cohen, Irving and Piliouras introduce doubly-efficient debate, in which two polynomial-time provers compete so that any polynomial-time computation can be verified with a constant number of human-judgement queries. Brown-Cohen et al. (2025) build a new recursive debate protocol on this line of work that, under stability assumptions, keeps the honest debater's required efficiency comparable to its opponent's while addressing the obfuscated arguments problem that affects existing recursive protocols.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: debate protocols with efficient honest strategies, extended from doubly-efficient debate to recursive debate that resists obfuscated arguments

text: The authors introduce doubly-efficient debate, in which two polynomial-time provers compete to convince a much more efficient verifier of the correctness of a computation that depends on black-box access to human judgements. They prove that, under appropriate assumptions, any polynomial-time computation can be verified using only a constant number of queries to the black box representing human judgement, in time linear in the size of a single query.
title: Doubly-efficient debate: poly-time honest prover, constant human-judgement queries
